goal.title: Fall Creek 50K
goal.subtitle: 12-week trail 50K plan
goal.weekAtGlance: Mon rest · Tue upper body · Wed short easy or StairMaster · Thu key run · Fri rest · Sat easy trail + light legs · Sun long easy trail
rules: Most running stays conversational (RPE 2–3). Hike meaningful climbs before effort spikes.
Never make up a missed workout. Skip Wednesday first when work or recovery is rough.
Fuel runs longer than 75–90 minutes: start near 30–50 g carbohydrate per hour.
Pain that changes gait, swelling, ankle giving-way, or pain 3+/10: stop and get clinical guidance.
goal.stairMasterRule: At most once a week, replace—not add to—the Wednesday easy run with 20–30 minutes at full-conversation effort (RPE 3–4). Start at 20 minutes and do not lean on the rails.

routines.name: Saturday lower body
routines.schedule: After the easy Saturday run. Leave 2–3 good reps in reserve.

exercises.name: Step-up or split squat
exercises.cue: Slow down; drive through whole foot

rules: It must not make Sunday worse.
If Sunday feels worse, do one set or skip strength that week.
From October 31 onward, use the ankle routine only; no loaded lower-body session.

routines.name: Ankle stability
routines.schedule: Tuesday and after two easy runs. Barefoot only if comfortable and safe.

exercises.name: Single-leg balance
exercises.cue: Tall posture; light fingertip support is fine

exercises.name: Band eversion

rules: Stop for pain, swelling, repeated rolling or giving-way, or altered gait, and seek clinical guidance.

locations.name: Heartland Park / Stones River Greenway
locations.description: Smooth asphalt. Good for early trail-setting runs, weekday aerobic work, and controlled hills; it does not train uneven footing. Check current boardwalk/segment notices before a long through-run.

locations.name: Peeler Park
locations.description: Very flat river-bottom farmland. Use the hiking network for low-consequence natural-surface practice or the paved route for easy time on feet. Expect wet grass/mud after rain; stay off the dedicated horse trails.

locations.name: Shelby Bottoms primitive trails
locations.address: Forrest Green Trailhead, 2032 Forrest Green Dr, Nashville, TN 37216
locations.distance: 2.75-mi Cornelia Fort Trail + short dirt spurs; 5.5 mi paved
locations.description: Mostly flat floodplain dirt/mulch with roots, grass and paved bailouts. Start with 20–40 minutes mixing dirt and greenway. It gets muddy after rain; the boardwalk near the observation deck is currently closed.

locations.name: Bells Bend — Loop + old farm roads
locations.address: Bells Bend Outdoor Center, 4187 Old Hickory Blvd, Nashville, TN 37218
locations.distance: 2.3-mi loop; repeat 4.6/6.9 mi or add farm-road branches
locations.description: Earthen, mown grass and gravel across gentle rolling fields. A strong terrain-effort match for Fall Creek and easy to shorten or repeat. expect sun, ticks and mud after rain.

locations.name: Long Hunter — Day Loop / Volunteer Trail
locations.address: Bakers Grove trailhead, 1594 Bakers Grove Rd, Hermitage, TN 37076
locations.distance: Day Loop 4.5 mi; Volunteer Trail 6 mi one-way
locations.description: Wooded dirt, limestone, roots and repeated modest rises. A useful all-around Sunday trail venue once you have a few smooth-dirt outings. Repeat/extend for longer days; stay conservative when wet.

locations.name: Percy Warner — Warner Woods
locations.address: Deep Well Trailhead, 6921 Highway 100, Nashville, TN 37221
locations.distance: 2.5-mi loop; pair with Mossy Ridge for about 7 mi
locations.description: Primitive wooded loop across ridges and valleys. More climbing and rock/root exposure than Long Hunter, so use after you are comfortable on trails. Stay on pedestrian hiking trails—not mountain-bike or bridle trails.

locations.name: Beaman Park — Henry Hollow / Laurel Woods
locations.address: Creekside/Highland, 4111 Little Marrowbone Rd, Joelton, TN 37080
locations.distance: Henry Hollow 2 mi; later 7.5 mi via shortcut or 12.5 full
locations.description: Rugged ridges, steep slopes, hollows and a creek crossing. Begin with Henry Hollow; use longer Laurel Woods only after trail durability is established. Great for hiking/downhill strength, but steeper and more remote than the race.

locations.name: Heartland hill repeats
locations.address: Heartland Park, 3135 Heartland Dr, Nashville, TN 37214
locations.distance: Repeat the main paved hill; build a 30–60 min session
locations.description: Useful Thursday hill substitute: power-hike hard enough to stay controlled, then jog/walk easily down. Paved and close, but it does not replace downhill trail-footing practice.

locations.name: Percy Warner — Mossy Ridge
locations.address: Deep Well Trailhead, 6921 Highway 100, Nashville, TN 37221
locations.distance: 4.25–4.5-mi loop; combine Warner Woods for about 7 mi
locations.description: Continuous wooded ridge/hollow climbing with roots, rocks and a steep rocky section. Use occasionally for climb/descent strength—not to imitate race pace. Stay on pedestrian hiking trails only.

locations.name: Radnor Lake — Ganier Ridge / South Cove — hike only
locations.address: Walter Criley Visitor Center, 1160 Otter Creek Rd, Nashville, TN 37220
locations.distance: Ganier Ridge 1.65 mi; South Cove 1.4 mi; connect carefully
locations.description: Steep, strenuous natural-surface hiking for power-hiking economy and careful foot placement. Running/jogging is prohibited on natural trails; run only on Otter Creek Road. Parking fills early.
